chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad Al-Hannat, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who was killed and had a father, a mother, and a son. The son said, "I want to kill the killer of my father," and another said, "I pardon," and another said, "I want to take the blood money."

He عليه السلام said: "Then the son should give the mother of the slain one-sixth of the blood money, and give the heirs of the killer one-sixth of the blood money as the right of the father who pardoned, and then kill him."

key_terms.أَعْفُو: I pardon; relinquishing the right to retaliatory punishment
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money paid in compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.السُّدُسَ: one-sixth, the fractional share due in this case
key_terms.حَقَّ الْأَبِ الَّذِي عَفَا: the right-share of the father who pardoned
key_terms.قَاتِلَ أَبِي: the killer of my father, referring to the offender liable for retaliation
key_terms.وَرَثَةَ الْقَاتِلِ: the heirs of the killer, who receive the relevant financial share

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if some heirs demand qiṣāṣ while others pardon or seek diyyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for qiṣāṣ when the heirs of a murder victim differ in their demands. If one heir seeks retaliation, another pardons, and another wants the diyyah, the one pursuing retaliation must compensate the others for their shares before carrying out the killing of the murderer.
